The public homepage was just simplified for new users (see PRODUCT.md), so the evidence moved off it. This page is where a judge verifies every claim in one place within 60 seconds.

READ FIRST (all in the repo): PRODUCT.md, README.md (focus-area table, results table, "What Broke While Building"), hackathon.md (Built in Public table, Demo, Upstream PRs), evidence/README.md (claim to proof map), evidence/neatlogs.md, evidence/entire.md, evidence/before_after_traces.json, evidence/trace-recovered-entire-v2.md, evidence/jury-selftest.txt, business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md, docs/data/plan.json, docs/data/prs.json, docs/index.html (design tokens, nav include docs/assets/site-nav.js, footer, three-band look), docs/receipts/ (sample receipts). Also the rubric notes: D:\Atharva\NOTES\PROJECTS\NeatHack - 10 October\21 Grading Checklist and Judge Map.md and 37 Rubric Gap Audit Sun.md and 02 Judges and Mentors.md (read-only; do not copy their internal strategy, advice or private notes onto the public page).

Invoke the Skill `impeccable` and follow it for a BRAND-register page: calm, precise, Apple-like, LIGHT mode, real logos (assets exist under docs/assets for neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai; check), no em dashes, no side-stripe borders, no gradient text, no identical card grids, honor prefers-reduced-motion. Site rules from the owner: every H2 centered, AP Title Case, NO subtitle under any H2; every content link underlined; most things centered; short plain copy; each major section has its own tinted background (use a calm distinct tint for this page, for example a cool slate or sage family, still one family with the site).

WHAT THE PAGE MUST DO
1. A 30-second path at the top: three or four links in order ("Watch the 3-minute demo", "Open a real receipt", "Read the before and after table", "Open the recovered trace evidence"). Large, centered, underlined, obvious.
2. THE PROOF MAP (the core): one clear block per rubric category in score order: The Agent (30%): the eight focus areas, each with the file or span that shows it (use the README focus-area table, link the real files on GitHub as https://github.com/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/blob/main/<path>). neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai (25%): a clear role for each, with the exact proof: neatlogs (traces per run, 2 detections, Investigate result, 2 evaluators that scored real traces, the before and after table; cite evidence/neatlogs.md and the numbers in evidence/before_after_traces.json), Entire (checkpoints behind commits: use the TRUE count from evidence/entire.md, the public commit page link https://entire.io/gh/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/commit/3ca6f118ecb0a8915315eea27b5588dd8a7c6299, graph evidence, jury self-test score; state plainly that Trail pages need an Entire login), cfo.ai (the public model https://cfo.ai/s/_u5lbrHIl9KX_JQE, business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md, the cap per tier, and that every cost comes from neatlogs traces in business/drivers.csv). Demo video (20%): the YouTube link https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JJNWWhSV9pc with its length as stated in hackathon.md. Building in public (15%): link to the real posts from the hackathon.md table (read the real URLs there; use only posts that exist and are tagged). Usefulness and originality (10%): the 4 upstream PRs (docs/data/prs.json), the Doc-audit boards, the receipts.
3. THE SEVEN CLAIMS: a short checklist of the seven claims judges are told to verify (agent improved, neatlogs used, Entire used, cfo.ai used, recovery shown, built in public, code written during the event with the first commit time from hackathon.md), each with one underlined link to its proof and a one-line honest note where the proof has a caveat (for example 74 of 88 normal commits carry a checkpoint trailer, read the exact current numbers from evidence/entire.md, do not guess).
4. "WHAT BROKE" (honest failure log): 3 to 5 lines taken from README "What Broke While Building" and hackathon.md, each with a number. Judges trust failures with numbers.
5. THE ONE-MINUTE REPRODUCE: the exact install and run commands from the README quickstart (pip install, firstrun run URL) in a copyable code block with a copy button, plus the pytest line and the test count from the README badge/proof.
6. Footer link back to the homepage. Add a discreet "For judges" link to the homepage footer in docs/index.html (one line; do not touch anything else there) and to docs/assets/site-nav.js only if it can be added as a plain nav link without breaking layout (check the nav at 1280 and 375 px; skip it if it crowds).

TRUTH RULES (very important): every number, count, date and URL on this page must come from a file in the repo or from a link you checked. Verify each external URL with curl (HTTP 200 logged out) and each GitHub blob path exists in the repo. Do not invent metrics. Do not claim a trace is public unless the file says so. If a proof file is missing, leave that item out and tell me in your report instead of making something up. No private strategy, no mentions of other judges' opinions, no advice-to-self copy.

BUILD AND CHECK: static HTML, CSS inline or in a small file under docs/judges/, vanilla JS only for the copy button. Fast, accessible (landmarks, focus states, AA contrast), responsive to 375 px with no sideways scroll. Serve with `py -3.11 -m http.server <free port> --directory <worktree>\docs` and verify at 1280, 768 and 375 px; take screenshots (headless Edge works: `& "C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe" --headless=new --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars --window-size=1280,2400 --screenshot=<ABSOLUTE WINDOWS PATH>\x.png <url>`; relative paths fail). Critique your own screenshots as a judge who has 60 seconds: do they find the proof for each category? Iterate. Add an offline test only if the repo has a pattern for static pages (check tests/); otherwise skip.

COMMIT: on your branch. The commit hook can hang: run `git commit` in the background (`(git commit -m "..." > log 2>&1 &)`), wait about 20 s, then in PowerShell stop ONLY the stuck process: `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='entire.exe'" | ? { $_.CommandLine -match 'prepare-commit-msg' } | % { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force }`, confirm with `git log`. Never --no-verify, never Co-Authored-By.

REPORT BACK: branch and commit, the page's sections, every external link you verified with its status, anything you left out because proof was missing, and anything a judge could still not verify. Be exact.

You are in a stronger position than your notes say. I read your NOTES rubric files and checked the repo and live links against them.

|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | All 8 focus areas have code and a span. Before and after: 2 of 4 to 3 of 4 finished, $0.0262 to $0.0200 per run. |
| neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | Both evaluators scored real traces, 5 of 5 on the audit one. The cfo.ai model and the Entire commit page open logged out. |

| Building in public | 15% | 13 posts exist, 11 tagged #neatHack. |
| Usefulness | 10% | 4 upstream PRs are open and return 200 logged out. |

The risk is proof scattered across files. My homepage redesign also moved the evidence off the homepage. An Opus agent is building `/judges/` now. It is one page that maps each rubric category and each of the 7 claims to a proof link. It has a one-minute reproduce block and a short list of what broke, with numbers. Every number and link must come from a repo file or a link the agent checks. I will report when it is done.

**Only you can do these** (none of them is code):
1. **Confirm your team.** The hackathon page lists "Check in and confirm your team" as step 3. Miss it and nothing else counts. Also check the award form. About 10 minutes.
2. **Make one neatlogs trace public.** Trace `5520c5cff5e0ea61f130eced082b20c4`, the recovered Entire run. Judges currently see trace IDs, not a link. About 10 minutes.
3. **Approve the 9 ready X and LinkedIn posts.** Each has a number and a failure, and each passed the gates. The send-order list and the commands are in file 38. Say "schedule the posts" and I run them row by row.
4. **Submit between 7:00 and 7:05 PM IST on Monday.** The "Submit on X" button appears only in that window. The video link is ready for the quote post.

**My part:** merge [PR #50](https://github.com/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/pull/50) so judges see the cleaner site. Open its preview and say "merge it".

"""Estimate the Jev cost of audits that ran before cost tracking, by re-running each one today.

An audit board in docs/audits/<id>.json that has no `cost` gets one, marked `estimated`. The numbers
come from a real re-run of the same audit (same repo, same docs repo), so they are measured Jev usage
for an equivalent audit, not a guess. The re-run publishes nothing: it only reads the cost counters.

    python scripts/audit_cost_estimates.py            # print what would be measured
    python scripts/audit_cost_estimates.py --apply    # re-run, write cost into the boards, then
                                                      # run `firstrun receipt --all-published`

Needs git, network and TYPESAFE_API_KEY (read from .env in the folder you run it from).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from firstrun import audit as audit_mod  # noqa: E402

SITE = ROOT / "docs" / "audits"


def basis(today: str) -> str:
    return (f"Estimate. This audit ran before cost tracking. Re-running the same audit on {today} used this much Jev "
            "input, billed at TypeSafe's list price of $0.042 per million input tokens. Output is free, and the clone "
            "and the analysis are free.")


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--apply", action="store_true", help="Re-run the audits and write the estimates.")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    todo = []
    for p in sorted(SITE.glob("audit-*.json")):
        board = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if not board.get("cost"):
            todo.append((p, board))
    for p, b in todo:
        print(f"{'measure' if args.apply else 'would measure'} {b['repo']}" + (f" (docs in {b['docs_repo']})" if b.get("docs_repo") else ""))
    if not args.apply or not todo:
        print("dry run. Add --apply to re-run and write." if not args.apply else "nothing to estimate.")
        return 0
    today = date.today().isoformat()
    for p, b in todo:
        audit_mod._JEV_USE.update(calls=0, input_tokens=0)
        audit_mod.audit(b["repo"], stale_days=b.get("stale_days", 180), use_jev=True, docs_repo=b.get("docs_repo") or None)
        c = audit_mod.jev_cost()
        if not c["jev_calls"]:
            print(f"  {b['repo']}: Jev made no call, so no estimate was written (is TYPESAFE_API_KEY set?)")
            continue
        b["cost"] = {**c, "estimated": True, "basis": basis(today)}
        p.write_text(json.dumps(b, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"  {b['repo']}: {c['jev_calls']} calls, {c['jev_input_tokens']:,} tokens, ${c['jev_usd']:.6f}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

input.description: Restore per-tool evidence on homepage
input.prompt:
You are a senior product designer and front-end engineer. Restore the PER-TOOL EVIDENCE on the FirstRun homepage (docs/index.html, section id="tools") in a form that is clear, beautiful and fast. You work in a git worktree of D:\Atharva\firstrun. FIRST run `git fetch origin && git switch -c site/tool-evidence origin/main` inside your worktree. Commit on that branch. Do NOT push, open PRs or merge.

THE OWNER'S WORDS: "Evidence on how each of the tools was used is also missing. It was previously there. Please ensure it's on the homepage as well!" The current section ("Each Tool Caught a Real Problem in FirstRun") is only a logo row with one line per tool. The previous version had real screenshots and numbers for neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai. This is a hackathon entry (neatHack 2026, judged on how clearly each of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai is USED, with proof), so this evidence is worth real score and must look excellent, but the page was also just simplified because it confused new visitors: the evidence has to be easy to scan, never a wall of text or a log.

READ FIRST: PRODUCT.md and invoke the Skill `impeccable` (brand register; its laws apply: OKLCH, no em dashes, no side-stripe borders, no gradient text, no glassmorphism by default, no identical card grids, honor prefers-reduced-motion, ease-out). Site rules from the owner: every H2 centered, AP Title Case, NO subtitle under H2; every content link underlined; mostly centered; short plain copy; light mode. The section needs its own calm neutral background that fits next to the blue (Doc-test), purple (Doc-audit) and gold (Receipt) bands above it. Read docs/index.html (the current #tools section and the CSS/JS around it, plus the existing carousel and reveal approach to stay consistent), docs/assets/ (the screenshots: t-neatlogs-*.webp, t-entire-*.webp, t-cfo-ari.webp, shot-*.webp, logo-*.webp), evidence/README.md, evidence/neatlogs.md, evidence/entire.md, evidence/neatlogs-investigation.md, business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md and docs/receipts/ (a real receipt).

THE OLD EVIDENCE (from the previous page): `git show e41eb3b:docs/index.html`, search for `xyz:[` and `img:"assets/t-` (around lines 1015 to 1040). It lists, per tool, three headline claims and a set of screenshots with captions, for example neatlogs: recovery in the span tree, a custom detection, detection analysis, Investigate (52.8x spike in Execution Failed, root cause with confidence), Docs Bisect trace (5 probes, last good 0.3.1, first bad 0.4.6), analytics; Entire: Trail board, analytics, merge gate, review findings, inline review, checkpoint on a commit; cfo.ai: Ari on day one, the 18-month model (cfo.ai/s/_u5lbrHIl9KX_JQE), the old $0.50 cap runs out of cash in month 14 so the plan sets the cap. Some of those numbers may be stale: VERIFY EVERY NUMBER against the current files (evidence/*.md, evidence/before_after_traces.json, business/*, docs/runs/index.json, docs/data/plan.json) and use the current true figure or drop the claim. Never invent a number.

WHAT TO BUILD
1. A tabbed (or segmented) showcase with three tools: neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai. Each tab carries the real logo, a one-line ROLE ("what this tool did for FirstRun"), and THREE pieces of evidence chosen as the strongest and most distinct per tool. Each evidence item = a real screenshot (existing asset, lazy-loaded, sized with width/height to avoid layout shift, sharp on retina) plus ONE caption line that contains a real number, plus an underlined link to the source of truth (the GitHub evidence file, the public cfo.ai model, the Entire commit page https://entire.io/gh/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/commit/3ca6f118ecb0a8915315eea27b5588dd8a7c6299 , a receipt). Pick the three per tool that a judge would find most convincing: e.g. neatlogs = Investigate with root cause, the recovery span tree, detection analysis or Docs Bisect; Entire = a checkpoint on a commit, the merge gate that blocked a risky merge, review findings caught before merge; cfo.ai = the plan that sets the cost cap (consider the model chart from docs/plan/ or docs/data/cfo-model.json drawn small, or the sample receipt, or Ari), with the month-14 finding. A large focused screenshot on one side and the three evidence items as a clear numbered selector on the other works well; the clicked item swaps the screenshot with a smooth cross-fade. Mobile: stack, with a swipeable or tappable selector, no sideways page scroll.
2. Show the three tools' names and logos always, so a visitor sees all three at a glance even before choosing a tab. The default tab is neatlogs. Keep deep links working (for example #tools-entire opens the Entire tab).
3. A single closing underlined link row: "See all the proof for judges" pointing to ./judges/ if that page exists on origin/main when you finish (another agent is building docs/judges/index.html on a parallel branch; check `git fetch origin` and `git ls-tree origin/main docs/judges/`; if it does not exist yet, link to the repo's evidence folder https://github.com/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/tree/main/evidence instead and tell me).
4. No-JS fallback: all three tools stacked, every screenshot visible. Accessibility: proper tablist/tab/tabpanel semantics, arrow-key navigation, visible focus, AA contrast, alt text that states what the screenshot proves, images lazy-loaded below the fold, no layout-property animation, reduced motion respected. Fast: no libraries, no large new assets (reuse the webp files; if one needs a tighter crop, make a small optimized derivative).
5. Keep H2 copy short, centered, AP Title Case, no subtitle (you may keep the existing H2 or write a stronger plain one).

CONCURRENCY: two other agents edit docs/index.html in other places in parallel (the hero at the top, and a footer link). Touch ONLY the #tools section and its CSS/JS blocks. Before your final commit run `git fetch origin` and merge origin/main into your branch; resolve conflicts so every change survives.

VERIFY: serve your worktree docs folder (`py -3.11 -m http.server <free port> --directory <worktree>\docs`) and test in real browsers. Headless Edge screenshots work with ABSOLUTE Windows paths (`& "C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe" --headless=new --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars --window-size=1440,1200 --virtual-time-budget=6000 --screenshot=<ABSOLUTE PATH>\x.png <url>`); tab and hover states need a driven browser (Playwright over node, the Claude_Browser tools, or DevTools protocol on headless Edge). Capture the section at 1440, 1024, 768 and 375 px in each tab, plus keyboard focus, plus the no-JS view. Check console errors, sideways scroll, layout shift, image weights. Critique honestly against the owner's words and the judges' needs: can a judge see, in 15 seconds, how each of the three tools was actually used and verify it? Iterate until yes. Run `PYTHONPATH=src py -3.11 -m pytest -q` before committing.

COMMIT: on your branch. The commit hook can hang: run `git commit` in the background (`(git commit -m "..." > log 2>&1 &)`), wait about 20 s, then in PowerShell stop ONLY the stuck process: `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='entire.exe'" | ? { $_.CommandLine -match 'prepare-commit-msg' } | % { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force }`, confirm with `git log`. Never --no-verify, never Co-Authored-By.

REPORT BACK: branch and commit; the final copy (H2, each tool's role line, each evidence caption and its source link); which numbers you verified against which file and any you changed or dropped; screenshots (absolute paths); accessibility and performance notes; anything unfinished. Be exact.

Another Opus agent will execute your plan, so be concrete: exact files, functions, data schemas, formulas, UI structure. Read the real code and data before planning: src/firstrun/audit.py (git history reading, read_history, find_features, momentum, build_cards, the `cards`/`features`/`pages`/`history` result fields, publish(), jev usage), src/firstrun/cli.py (audit commands), scripts/audit_intake.py and .github/workflows/audit-request.yml (the CI path that audits public repos on GitHub Actions), docs/doc-audit/index.html (the whole board UI: header, bar, the "What to Ship Next" four-column board with the drawer), docs/audits/*.json and docs/audits/index.json (7 real published audits: fastapi/typer, AltimateAI/altimate-code, entireio/cli, dbt-labs/dbt-core with docs repo dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com, OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator, neatlogs/neatlogs, AccuKnox/help), tests/test_audit.py and tests/test_intake.py, PRODUCT.md (design principles: calm, precise, Apple-like, light mode, one idea per section, H2s centered with NO subtitle, links underlined, never confusing) and docs/index.html for the visual language (three tinted bands, receipt bill, prism hero is being added elsewhere).

THE OWNER'S REQUEST (verbatim intent):
(1) In the Doc-audit "What to Ship Next" board the "Create Content" column "looks very silly, is not accurate and does not show real, valuable info" (it lists 'areas' like mkdocs, build, post, edit_template with '1 commit' each). Also "Document This" and "Create Content" "should be a single column ideally". Replace it with: "the TOP 10 PRIORITIZED issues to pick up next, with rationale".
(2) A team map: "show which user or contributor from GitHub has expertise in which part of the app so the relevant issues can be assigned to people who show proficiency in some part of the codebase: map the users to the task and show the distribution of that visually: team member X works most on Y, and suggest which issues to be picked by which team member. All this can be done via the GitHub contributor details." Place it "near the top of the audit page, before What to Ship Next, in a very amazing manner. This has to be visually amazing!"

WHAT YOUR PLAN MUST COVER
A. DATA MODEL (additive to audit.json schema v1; old boards must keep rendering): a `team` block and a `next` (top-10) block. Define exactly the fields. The audit already clones the repo (blobless, full history) and `read_history` yields per-commit author info and changed files: decide what author identity the history gives (name, email) and how to derive a GitHub login and avatar WITHOUT secrets: for example the `ID+login@users.noreply.github.com` noreply form, and optionally the GitHub REST API (`gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/contributors`, and commit author lookup) when a token exists (it does in GitHub Actions and on the owner's machine via `gh auth`), with a no-token fallback to initials and a deterministic color. Never publish email addresses on the public boards; hash or drop them. Exclude bots (dependabot, renovate, github-actions, copilot, *-bot, [bot]) and optionally merge commits. Merge identities that are clearly the same person (same login or same normalized name).
B. EXPERTISE ALGORITHM: define AREAS of the codebase (top-level directories or the existing `area` classification used by features and cards; for repos where docs live in a second repo such as dbt-core + docs.getdbt.com, say how areas map across both repos), and a recency-weighted expertise score per (person, area): for example exponential decay with a half-life of about 90 days on commits, weighted by lines or files changed with caps, normalized so one giant commit cannot dominate; derive `works most on`, `share of area`, `last active`, `bus factor` per area (how many people hold more than 20% of recent weight), and flag single-owner areas. Give the formulas and the thresholds, and justify them. Handle small repos (1 to 3 contributors), huge repos (hundreds of contributors: show top N plus an "everyone else" bucket), one-person repos (the map must still be meaningful and honest), and areas with no recent activity.
C. TOP 10 PRIORITIZED ISSUES with rationale: build them from the signals the audit already has (stale pages with commits since last edit, shipped user-facing features with no docs, momentum areas, release notes missing, quickstart check) and rank with an explicit scoring formula (impact for readers, urgency/staleness, effort, evidence strength, whether Jev judged it). Each item: a title in plain words, a one-sentence RATIONALE that cites its evidence (commit short SHAs, dates, counts), a priority score and a human-readable "why now", an effort estimate (S, M, L) with its rule, the suggested owner (person with the highest expertise in the touched area, tie-broken by recent activity and by balancing load so one person is not assigned everything), the runner-up, and a one-line reason ("Maya made 14 of the last 20 commits to docs/use-cases"). Only real data. If no one has expertise, say "no clear owner" and suggest the most recent toucher.
D. UI SPEC (this is the star: "visually amazing"): propose and justify the best visualization of "who works on what". Evaluate options such as a contributor by area heatmap matrix, a ribbon/chord or Sankey from people to areas, an arc or radial map, avatar-bubbles clustered by area, a stacked bar per area showing ownership share, a swimlane. Choose a primary view and a secondary view, specify the layout in detail (sizes, order, grouping, color system consistent with the site, labeling so a stranger understands it in 5 seconds without a legend lecture), hover and focus interactions (hover a person to highlight their areas and their suggested tasks; hover an area to see its owners), the connection to the Top 10 list (each item shows a small avatar of its suggested owner; clicking an owner filters the list to their picks), a bus-factor callout, empty and loading and error states, small-repo and huge-repo behavior, dark/light (site is light), responsive down to 375 px, keyboard and screen-reader support (tables or lists with the same information as text), reduced motion, performance (inline SVG or CSS grid, no libraries, board JSON size budget), and how the section is placed: after the board header and summary bar, BEFORE the ship-next list, with a centered H2 and no subtitle. The ship-next board becomes ONE column: the ranked top 10 as a clean list (rank number, title, rationale, evidence chips, effort, owner avatar), with the old kind filters kept only if they add value; say what happens to the other card kinds (refresh, feature, document, quickstart, automate) so nothing real is lost, and how the drawer that shows the commits behind a card is kept.
E. BACKFILL AND CI: how the 7 published boards get `team` and `next` WITHOUT re-running Jev or republishing changed counts (a script that re-clones, computes only the new blocks and writes them into docs/audits/<id>.json, in the style of scripts/audit_cost_estimates.py), how `firstrun audit` and the intake workflow produce them for new audits (GitHub token availability in Actions: GITHUB_TOKEN), rate-limit handling, caching, timeouts, and failure behavior (the audit must never fail because the contributor lookup failed).
F. PRIVACY AND ETHICS: this puts named people next to tasks on a public page. State what is shown (public commit authorship only, GitHub login and avatar, no emails), how a repo owner or a person can opt out (for example a `team: false` option, an env flag, a CLI flag `--no-team`), the wording that frames suggestions as suggestions, and that private-repo audits keep the board private as today.
G. TESTS: offline pytest plan with small synthetic git repos built in tmp_path (multiple authors, bots, noreply emails, renamed files, merge commits, a one-person repo, a repo with 300 authors), asserting the scores, the owner suggestion, load balancing, no emails in output, schema additivity (old board JSON still renders), and the front-end data contract.
H. WORK BREAKDOWN: an ordered list of steps with files touched, so one executing agent (or two in parallel: backend data, frontend UI) can implement and verify it. List risks, open questions that truly block, and a definition of done with how to verify in a browser (desktop 1280, tablet 768, phone 375) using the real published boards.

Be decisive: where there are options, pick one and say why. Keep the plan precise and compact enough to execute (aim for a document an engineer can follow without asking you anything). Do not write code files, but include short code or pseudo-code for the formulas and the JSON schema.

## 0. Read this first

**Uncommitted work is in the tree.** Branch `feat/audit-cost-estimates` has uncommitted edits to:
- `docs/doc-audit/index.html`
- `docs/audits/audit-20261010-163{257,411,526}-*.json`

- the untracked `scripts/audit_cost_estimates.py`

Those changes add the `est.` receipt chip and estimated costs. Commit and merge that branch first, then branch `feat/team-map` from the updated `main`. Never run the backfill while `audit_cost_estimates.py --apply` is running, because both rewrite whole board files.

**Do not touch these:**
- `docs/index.html`: the prism hero is being added there in another worktree.
- The `cards` array and `summary` of published boards: receipts list card counts in `work.cards`.

Receipts are not at risk from the backfill. Published audit receipts have `evidence_sha256: {}` and hash only `runs/` files, never `docs/audits/*.json`, so adding keys to a board does not break a receipt check.

**Never use `--numstat`, `--stat` or `-p` on an audit clone.** The clone is blobless, so any of these makes git download blobs for every commit. That is why expertise below is weighted by files changed, not by lines.

**Facts checked in the code and data:**
- `read_history` gives `sha`, committer date, author name (`%an`), subject and files (`--name-only --no-renames`). It has no email and no parent list.
- Merge commits already show no files because there is no `-m`.
- `features[].author` (names) is already public on every board.
- Only some boards have `history.head`. dbt, orchestrator, neatlogs and accuknox do not.
- `features[].area` is unreliable as a team area. Real accuknox values: `li`, `mkdocs`, `edit_template`.
- GraphQL `object(oid:)` returns the commit author's `user {login databaseId}`. I checked this live with `gh`.
- The intake workflow step already exports `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`.

**Bot accounts seen in the real repos:**
- `github-actions[bot]`, `dependabot[bot]`, `pre-commit-ci[bot]`, `latest-changes[bot]`, `altimate-harness-bot[bot]`, `neatlogs-release[bot]`
- `FishtownBuildBot`, `snyk-bot`, `Copilot`
- `fa-assistant`: a "User" account on dbt-core that looks like an automation account.

---

## A. Data model (additive to schema `v: 1`)

Two new top-level keys: `team` and `next`. Every other key stays byte-identical. Readers must treat both as optional.

```jsonc
"team": {
  "v": 1,
  "as_of": "2026-10-10",            // date part of generated_at; all decay is computed from here
  "window_days": 365, "half_life_days": 90,
  "source": "git+github",           // "git" when no GitHub lookup ran or it failed
  "commits": 1830,                  // human, non-merge, non-bulk commits in the window (both repos)
  "bots_skipped": 212,
  "total_people": 46,               // distinct humans in the window
  "people": [                       // sorted by recent weight, desc; index = color slot 0..11
    {"id":"p1","name":"Haider Rizvi","login":"sahrizvi","gh":1234567,"ini":"HR",
     "commits":140,"share":0.31,"last":"2026-10-09","top":"a2","top_share":0.55}
  ],                                // login and gh are null when unknown. No email, ever.
  "others": {"people":34,"commits":210,"share":0.12},   // null when everyone fits
  "areas": [
    {"id":"a1","label":"workspace","path":"packages/opencode/src/altimate/workspace/","repo":"code",
     "share":0.18,"commits":45,"last":"2026-10-09",
     "owners":[{"p":"p1","s":0.62},{"p":"p3","s":0.21}],   // up to 3, s >= 0.05; "p":"others" allowed
     "bus":2,"single":false,"quiet":false}
  ],
  "rest": {"share":0.07,"commits":60},   // weight outside the listed areas
  "cells": [[0,0,12.4],[0,2,3.1],[-1,1,2.0]]   // [person index (-1 = others), area index, recent weight, 2 dp]
}
// Opt-out instead of the block above: "team": {"v":1,"disabled":"flag"|"env"|"repo"}
// On failure, "team" is omitted.
```

```jsonc
"next": {
  "v": 1, "top": 10,
  "weights": {"impact":0.30,"urgency":0.25,"evidence":0.20,"judged":0.15,"ease":0.10},
  "items": [                         // ranked, at most 30; the UI shows 10, then "Show all"
    {"rank":1,"kind":"document",     // document | refresh | release | announce | quickstart
     "title":"Write a page for workspace","path":"","area":"a1",
     "rationale":"22 user-facing workspace changes shipped since Aug 24, 2026, newest c78b284e6 on Oct 6, and Jev found no docs page that explains them.",
     "why_now":"Shipped 4 days ago",
     "score":92,"parts":{"impact":1.0,"urgency":0.94,"evidence":1.0,"judged":1.0,"ease":0.3},
     "effort":"L","effort_why":"A new page that covers 22 changes",
     "judge":"jev","action":"<the card's action text>","count":22,
     "evidence":[{"sha":"c78b284e6","date":"2026-10-06","subject":"...","pr":"1381"}],   // at most 5
     "owner":{"p":"p1","why":"Haider Rizvi wrote 20 of the 22 changes behind it"},     // or null
     "runner_up":{"p":"p3","why":"Saravanan made 6 of the last 20 commits to packages/opencode/src/altimate/workspace/"},
     "balanced":false,             // true when load balancing moved it away from the top expert
     "fallback":""                 // when owner is null: "Last touched by Ashok on Jul 3, 2026"
    }
  ]
}
```

**Contract rules:**
- Every `owner.p` and `runner_up.p` is an id in `team.people`. If a chosen owner is outside the top 12, append them, up to 16 people.
- `cells` indexes are in range.
- Size budget: `team` under 10 KB, `next` under 25 KB.
- With `team` disabled or absent, owners are `null` and `next` is still produced.
- Sitemap mode produces `next` (refresh items scored on age only, no owners) and no `team`.

**Old card kind to new item kind:** `document` → `document`, `refresh` → `refresh`, `automate` → `release`, `feature` → `announce`, `quickstart` → `quickstart`. `content` is dropped.

New audits stop emitting `content` cards: delete that block in `build_cards`. The momentum signal behind them moves into the `next` impact score and into the team map's area activity.

---

## B. Team: identity, expertise, areas

**New module: `src/firstrun/team.py`**

### B1. History fields (additive, in `audit.py`)

- `read_history(repo, rev="HEAD")` uses the format `%x01%H%x09%cI%x09%aI%x09%P%x09%an%x09%ae%x09%s` and `split("\t", 6)`.
- It adds the keys `email`, `adate` (author date) and `parents` (count). `date`, `author`, `subject`, `files` and `scope` stay unchanged.
- `read_tags` adds `tagger` (`%(taggername)`). It stays empty for lightweight tags.
- Emails are used only inside `team.py` and are never written anywhere.

### B2. Which commits count

A commit counts only if all of these hold:
- `parents <= 1` (merges are skipped).
- `adate` is within 365 days of `as_of`.
- The author is not a bot.
- It touches 300 files or fewer. Bigger commits are mass imports, formatting runs or Copybara drops ("Project import generated by Copybara." is in dbt).

Files are dropped by `TEAM_SKIP`:
- Hidden dirs: `(^|/)\.[^/]+/`. This covers `.github`, `.changes`, `.claude`, `.changeset`.
- `(^|/)(node_modules|vendor|third_party|dist|build|out|target)/`
- Lockfiles and snapshots: `\.lock$`, `-lock\.json$`, `lock\.ya?ml$`, `go\.sum$`, `\.snap$`
- Generated files: `\.min\.(js|css)$`, `\.pb\.go$`, `_pb2\.py$`
- `(^|/)(changelog|changes|history)(\.[a-z]+)?$` (case-insensitive)

### B3. Bots

`is_bot(name, email, login)` is true if any of these match:
- Login, email local part, or name ends with `[bot]`.
- Login or email local part ends with `bot`. So does a name with no spaces (this catches `dependabot`, `FishtownBuildBot`, `snyk-bot`). A spaced name like "Sam Talbot" is safe.
- Lowercased name or login is in a known list: `github-actions, dependabot, renovate, copilot, copilot-swe-agent, pre-commit-ci, greenkeeper, codecov, mergify, semantic-release-bot, allcontributors, claude, devin-ai-integration, cursoragent, codex, web-flow`.
- Email is `noreply@github.com`, `actions@github.com`, or `*@anthropic.com` when the name is Claude.
- Login, or a name with no spaces, matches `(^|[-_])(assistant|automation)$`. This catches `fa-assistant`.
- Login or name is in `bots` of `docs/audits/team-optout.json` (see F).

### B4. Identity and merging

Parse emails:
- `^(\d+)\+([^@]+)@users\.noreply\.github\.com$` → gh id and login.
- `^([^@+]+)@users\.noreply\.github\.com$` → login.

When a token exists, run the GitHub lookup:
- Take the newest commit sha of each identity (distinct lowercased email). Limit this to the top 100 identities by weight.
- Query `https://api.github.com/graphql` in batches of 50: `c{i}: object(oid:"<hex>"){... on Commit{author{user{login databaseId}}}}`, with `repository(owner,name)` taken from the clone URL. Validate that each oid is hex.
- Token: `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GH_TOKEN`, else `gh auth token` (subprocess, 5 s timeout, never logged).
- Each call uses `httpx` with a 15 s timeout. Stop after 4 calls. Skip the lookup if the `X-RateLimit-Remaining` header is under 50.
- Any exception returns `{}` and sets `source = "git"`. Keep an in-process memo only and no disk cache: at most 4 calls per audit, so a cache adds risk and saves nothing.

Merge identities with union-find:
- Same login, or same lowercased email.
- Same normalized name: NFKD, accents stripped, casefold, punctuation removed, whitespace collapsed. Skip the name merge when the two identities have different known logins, or the name is generic (`root, admin, ubuntu, user, unknown, github, dev`).

Display values:
- Name: the most-used git name. If it contains `@`, use the login. If there is no login, use `Contributor N`.
- `ini`: first letters of the first two name tokens, else the first two characters of the login.

Without a token, "Victor Gutierrez" and "Victor Gutierrez Calderon" (entireio) stay separate. With a token they merge through the login `gtrrz-victor`. That is acceptable.

### B5. Recency-weighted file weight

```
decay(c)  = 2 ** (-(as_of - c.adate).days / 90)
n         = len(kept_files(c))
mass(c)   = decay(c) * min(1 + log2(n), 4)       # 1 file = 1, 2 = 2, 4 = 3, 8 or more = 4
share(c,f)= mass(c) / n                          # spread evenly over the commit's files
```

Why these numbers:
- **Half-life 90 days.** A quarter is the usual planning cycle. A one-year-old commit counts 6%, so people who left fade out and steady contributors stay.
- **Window 365 days.** Older commits weigh under 6%. Cutting them keeps the run fast.
- **Log cap.** A 250-file refactor counts at most 4 one-file fixes, spread thinly. No single commit can dominate.
- **Files, not lines.** Line counts need blobs, which the clone does not have.

Accumulate:
- `w[p][f]` per file.
- `dw[p][(repo, dir)]` for every ancestor dir, up to depth 6.

### B6. Areas: the "frontier" split (decided, replaces `features[].area` for the team)

Inputs:
- `file_w[(repo, path)]`, summed over all humans.
- The set of dirs present at `as_of` (`git ls-tree -r --name-only <rev>`).

A path whose dir no longer exists maps to its longest existing ancestor. If it has none, it goes to `rest`. That also handles renames.

```
DESCEND = 0.85; SPLIT = 0.22; MIN = 0.03; AREAS_MAX = 10 (single repo) | code 7 + docs 3 (docs repo)
descend(n): while n has a child c with W(c) >= DESCEND*W(n): n = c       # skips src/, packages/x/src/, crates/
nodes = [descend(c) for c in children(root) if W(c) >= MIN*T]; root-level files and small children go to rest
loop:
  n = heaviest node with W(n) >= SPLIT*T and at least 2 child dirs with W >= MIN*T
  if none or len(nodes) >= AREAS_MAX: break
  replace n with [descend(c) for those children] + "n (other)" bucket if the remainder is >= MIN*T, else the remainder goes to rest
keep the heaviest AREAS_MAX nodes; the rest go to rest
label = basename(n); if basename is in {src, lib, app, core, internal, pkg, main, source, packages, crates, docs, content}: use "parent/basename"
```

When `docs_repo` is set, run the frontier separately per repo: `repo:"code"` with up to 7 areas and `repo:"docs"` with up to 3. Shares are within each repo. People merge across both repos by login or normalized name. In a single repo, docs dirs compete as normal areas (for accuknox: `docs/use-cases`, `docs/getting-started`, and so on).

### B7. Per-area and per-person metrics

| Field | Formula |
|---|---|
| `area.share` | `W(area) / T(repo)` |
| `owners[].s` | person's weight in the area / `W(area)`, over all humans, with `others` aggregated |
| `bus` | smallest k such that the top-k owner shares sum to at least 0.5 (classic truck factor) |
| `single` | top share >= 0.75, or only one person with share >= 0.05 |
| `quiet` | `as_of - area.last` > 180 days |
| `person.share` | person's weight / total human weight |
| `top` | the person's heaviest area |
| `top_share` | that area's weight / the person's total weight (including `rest`) |
| `commits`, `last` | raw counts and dates, shown to humans; ranking uses weights |

Why a truck factor and not the suggested ">20% holders" count: with ten people at 10% each, the >20% rule gives a bus factor of 0, which is wrong. Taking the fewest people who hold half the work stays meaningful at any team size.

Which people are listed:
- The top 12 by weight, and only those with share >= 1.5% or at least 3 commits.
- Everyone else goes into `others`.
- Owners and runners-up from `next` are appended, up to 16 in total.

Edge cases:
- **One person:** 1 person, every area `single`. The UI says so plainly (D).
- **1 to 3 people:** normal map.
- **Hundreds of people:** top 12 plus `others`. Test this at 300.
- **History capped at 20,000:** if the oldest commit is newer than the window start, set `team.capped = true`.

`build_team(sources, as_of, hidden=set(), extra_bots=set(), token=None) -> (team_json, ctx)`. The `ctx`, which is internal and never serialized, holds:
- `pid_of_sha[sha9]`
- `files_of_sha[sha9]`
- `dw`
- `recent_by_dir[(repo, dir)]`: the newest 20 human commits, as `(pid, date)`
- `last_toucher(repo, path) -> (name, date)`
- `active(pid)`: true if the last commit is within 180 days
- `momentum`

---

## C. Top 10 prioritized items with rationale

**New module: `src/firstrun/nextup.py`**

`build_next(board, ctx | None, as_of, mom, changelog_recent) -> dict`. Inputs are only what a board already holds (`cards`, `pages`, `features`, `release`) plus history. That makes new audits and the backfill share the same code.

### C1. Candidates

- Every non-`content` card, mapped by kind.
- Up to 10 extra `refresh` candidates: stale or unchecked pages not already in a refresh card, top by `relevant_since`. Their evidence is `page.evidence`.
- Join a refresh card to its page by path (the `Refresh <path>` title, or `cardPath` logic). Join features by `sha`.
- Join document clusters to all `features` with the same `area` and `covered == false`.
- Dedupe announces by cleaned subject; accuknox has "Add GCP organization onboarding guide" twice. Drop an announce whose sha already appears in a document item.

### C2. Score

All parts are in [0, 1]. `d(x)` means days between `as_of` and date `x`.

```
score = round(100 * (0.30*I + 0.25*U + 0.20*E + 0.15*J + 0.10*ease)),  ease: S=1, M=0.6, L=0.3

document cluster: I = 0.55 + 0.25*min(1, n/10) + 0.20*min(1, mom[area].commits/30)
                  U = 2**(-d(newest)/45)
                  E = min(1, n/5) * (1 if area_src == "scope" or any strong term else 0.85)
                  J = 1 if any feature.judge == "jev" else 0.6
document single:  I = 0.55 + 0.10*(has strong term)
                  U = 2**(-d/45)
                  E = 0.6 + 0.2*(strong term) + 0.2*(PR number)
                  J as above
refresh:          I = 0.45 + 0.25*entry(path) + 0.30*min(1, relevant_since/20)
                  U = 0.5*min(1, age_days/730) + 0.5*2**(-d(newest evidence)/90)
                  E = min(1, relevant_since/5)
                  J = 1 if judge == "jev" and status == "stale"; 0.6 if text only; 0.35 if unchecked
                  entry = 1 if the name matches readme|index|quickstart|getting[-_]started|install|introduction|overview, or path depth <= 2
release:          I = 0.5 + 0.15*(not changelog_recent); U = 2**(-d(release.date)/30)
                  E = min(1, commits/10); J = 0.6
                  skip when commits == 0
announce:         I = 0.25; U = 2**(-d/21); E = 0.5 + 0.2*(PR); J = 0.4
quickstart:       I = 0.4 + 0.3*(README or quickstart-like page is stale/unchecked/aging)
                  U = 0.3; E = 0.3; J = 0.5
```

Why the weights are ordered this way:
1. **Impact first:** docs exist for readers.
2. **Urgency second:** users are trying new features now, and a stale page misleads every visitor today.
3. **Evidence third:** prefer what can be proven.
4. **Judged fourth:** a model read the page, versus a text match.
5. **Ease last:** a tie-breaker that favors quick wins without letting trivia outrank real gaps.

Hand-checked against real boards:

| Board | Item | Score |
|---|---|---|
| altimate-code | `workspace` cluster | 92 |
| dbt-core | `databricks` cluster | 85 |
| dbt-core | `_versions-contracts.md` refresh | 82 |
| accuknox | `Process-based-asset-access` refresh | 72 |
| altimate-code | YOLO single | 67 |
| (any) | announce | about 55 |
| accuknox | `net-seg` refresh | 50 |

**Effort rules** (`effort_why` gives the rule in words):

| Kind | S | M | L |
|---|---|---|---|
| refresh | `relevant_since` <= 3 | <= 10 | more than 10 |
| document cluster, own page exists | | n <= 6 | otherwise |
| document cluster, new page | | otherwise | n >= 8 |
| document single | has `closest_page` | otherwise | |
| release, announce, quickstart | always | | |

For refresh, an `ancient` page moves up one level, capped at L.

**Order and caps:**
- Sort by score descending, then newest evidence, then title.
- Caps inside the top 10: refresh 5, document 5, announce 2, release 1, quickstart 1.
- Overflow continues at rank 11 and later. Keep at most 30 items.

### C3. Text, from real fields only

**Titles:**
- Cluster with its own page: "Add the new {area} changes to {basename}".
- Cluster with no page: "Write a page for {area}".
- Single: "Document: {Clean subject}".
- Refresh: "Update {page title}", with `path` set.
- Release: "Publish the {name} release notes".
- Announce: "Announce: {Clean subject}".
- Quickstart: "Prove the quickstart still runs".

**Rationale** (one sentence, always citing a SHA, a date or a count):
- Refresh: "Last edited {date}. Since then {k} commits changed code on its topic, newest {sha} on {date}, and Jev expects the page is now wrong." The last clause is "Jev did not read it" when Jev did not run.
- Single: "{sha} shipped "{subject}" on {date} in #{pr}, and Jev read {closest_page} and found it does not explain it."
- Release: "{n} commits landed between {prev} and {name} ({date}), and no changelog file changed in the last 60 days."
- Cluster: as in the schema example.

**why_now:**
- Document and announce: "Shipped 4 days ago", "Shipped 3 weeks ago", "Shipped 2 months ago".
- Refresh: "Code moved 32 days ago under a page last edited 680 days ago".
- Release: "v2.0.5 shipped 3 days ago".
- Quickstart: "A text audit cannot prove a run".

### C4. Owner suggestion

```
For each item, collect:
  code_dirs: parent dirs of the product files in its evidence commits (found by sha in history), plus feature.files
  docs_dir:  parent dir of path (refresh), closest_page (document), README (quickstart)
A(p) = share of the item's evidence commits authored by p
C(p) = sum over d in code_dirs of dw[p][d] / max over q of the same     (0 for everyone if that max < 1.0)
D(p) = dw[p][docs_dir], plus the file itself, / max over q              (same floor)
aff  = a*A + b*C + g*D, with (a, b, g):
       document (.50, .35, .15)   refresh (.25, .30, .45)   announce (.80, .20, 0)
       quickstart (0, 0, 1)
       release: if the newest tag's tagger is human, that person gets aff 1; otherwise A over the release range
eligible = active in the last 180 days
owner only if top aff >= 0.25
otherwise owner = null and fallback = last human toucher of path or evidence files:
       "Last touched by {name} on {date}", else "No one touched these files in the last year"
```

**Load balancing** applies to the top 10 only, in rank order:
- `cap = max(2, ceil(10 / n_eligible) + 1)`, where `n_eligible` counts people with aff >= 0.25 on any top item. There is no cap when `n_eligible <= 1`.
- The pool is the eligible people with `aff >= 0.6 * top_aff`. Pick the first one in the pool whose load is under the cap. If none, pick the top expert anyway: the cap is soft.
- Set `balanced = true` when the pick is not the top expert.
- `runner_up` is the best other eligible person with aff >= 0.15.

**Reason** (the strongest term wins):
- A: "{name} shipped it in #{pr}" or "{name} wrote {k} of the {n} changes behind it".
- C or D: "{name} made {k} of the last {m} commits to {dir}/". `dir` is the deepest ancestor with at least 5 window commits. `m = min(20, commits to dir)`.
- Release: "{name} tagged {tag}".

Each item's `area` is the area whose path is the longest prefix of the item's primary file.

## D. UI spec (`docs/doc-audit/index.html`)

### D1. Choice of visualization

I rejected these options:
- **Chord diagram:** unreadable to a stranger and bad at 375 px.
- **Classic Sankey:** small nodes make labels collide.
- **Avatar bubbles:** imprecise.
- **Swimlane:** reads like a log.
- **Heatmap:** precise but needs a color legend.

**Primary view (760 px and wider): tapered ribbon map.** It is three aligned columns: a people list in HTML, an SVG ribbon band, and an areas list in HTML.
- Every row has a fixed 52 px pitch, and every node bar is 36 px tall, so labels never collide.
- A ribbon's **left end** thickness is the share of that person's work ("X works most on Y").
- Its **right end** thickness is that person's share of the area ("who holds Y").

One shape answers both questions. The only key is two column headers: "People · share of their work" and "Parts of the code · share of the area".

**Secondary view (default and only view under 760 px): "By area" list.**
- One row per area: label, the path in faint mono, and a 12 px stacked ownership bar in person colors, with others in gray.
- Under the bar: owner avatars with percentages.
- A badge: "1 owner" (warn style) when `single`, otherwise "{bus} hold half".
- It is semantic HTML, so it also serves as a text equivalent.

Order: header, `.health` bar, then a new `<section id="r-team" class="tband">`, then "What to Ship Next".

**The heading:** a centered H2 "Who Works on What" with no subtitle. Add an `.hc` class: centered, `clamp(24px, 3vw, 30px)`, weight 700, letter-spacing -.03em.

**Inside the band, top to bottom:**
1. A white `.panel` card: radius 20, the homepage `--lift` shadow, padding 24.

**People column:** one `<button>` per person.

right: for each area, stack ribbons in person order; thickness = 36 * w / sum(area column)

### D5. Avatars, safety and states

**Avatar URLs** are built only client-side, from validated fields:
- `gh` (integer) → `https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/{gh}?s=64&v=4`
- else a login matching `^[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,39}$` → `https://github.com/{login}.png?size=64`
- else an initials disc in the person's color.

Images use `loading=lazy`, `alt=""` (the name sits next to them), and `onerror` swaps in initials. Never use a URL taken from the JSON.

**States:**
- No `team`, or `team.disabled`: hide the section.
- Wrap `paintTeam` in try/catch. On error, hide the section and `console.warn`.
- No separate loading state: the board JSON already holds everything.
- Validate the `cells` index range and skip bad rows.

**Responsive:**
- 1280 px: full map.
- 768 px: the map still fits (520 px of columns).

- People and areas are native buttons with `aria-label`, for example "Haider Rizvi, 140 commits in the last year, works most on workspace. Show their suggested tasks."

- Single owner is shown with a text badge, never color alone.
- Text uses `--ink` and `--mut` for AA contrast.

**Motion:**
- Ribbons enter with a 500 ms opacity and scaleX from the left, with a 12 ms stagger.

**Performance:**
- At most 13x11 paths. Hover toggles classes only.
- On a width change, a 150 ms debounced ResizeObserver redraws only the SVG.
- No libraries.

**Theme:** light mode only (`color-scheme: light`), with all colors from variables.

## E. Backfill and CI

### E1. Backfill script: `scripts/audit_team_backfill.py` (same style as `audit_cost_estimates.py`)

Options:
- Default is a dry run that prints, per board: people, areas, the top 10 titles, owner, score.
- `--apply` writes.
- `--only <id>`, `--force` (recompute even if `team` exists), `--no-github`.

For each `docs/audits/audit-*.json` where `mode != "sitemap"`:
1. Clone with `audit.clone` into a temp dir.
2. `rev = history.head`, or `git rev-list -1 --before=<generated_at> HEAD`.
3. `commits = read_history(repo, rev)` and `tags = read_tags`. Get the paths at `rev` with `ls-tree`. Do the same for `docs_repo`.
4. `as_of = generated_at`.
5. `mom = audit.momentum(commits, as_of, board["features"])`. Compute `changelog_recent` the way `_audit` does.
6. Build `team` and `next`.
7. Set `b2 = {**b, "team": ..., "next": ...}`. Assert that `set(b2) - set(b) <= {"team", "next"}` and that every other value is equal.
8. Write compact JSON exactly like `publish()`. Never touch `index.json`, `cards`, `summary` or receipts.
9. Apply opt-outs (F). Remove the temp dir in `finally`.

No Jev call happens, so no counts change.

### E2. New audits

**`_audit`:**
- Add `team: bool = True`.
- After `build_cards`, wrap a `neatlogs.trace("audit.team", kind="TOOL")` in `try/except Exception`. On failure: no `team`, `next` built with `ctx=None`, and the span output records only the exception type.
- The trace output holds counts only, and `_trace_output` adds `next` titles and scores, never names.

**Opt-out checks:** `FIRSTRUN_TEAM=0` gives `disabled: "env"`. A repo file gives `disabled: "repo"` (F).

**CLI:** `firstrun audit --no-team`.

**Intake workflow:** `GH_TOKEN` already reaches `scripts/audit_intake.py`. Pass `team=fields["team"]`.

**Example workflow:** add `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` to the audit step in `examples/github-action/firstrun-audit.yml`.

**Output changes:**
- `to_markdown` adds "## What to Ship Next" (the top 10, with "Suggested: Name") and "## Who Works on What" (area → top owners).
- `issue()` uses `next.items[:10]` when present (fallback: cards, skipping `content`). Each line is `- [ ] **{title}**{ (`path`)}. {rationale} Suggested: {name} ({login}).` Write logins without `@` so nobody gets pinged.

**Failure behavior:** the token lookup, GraphQL, the opt-out file read and team math each fail closed to "no team" or `source: "git"`. The audit never fails because of them. The repo opt-out read is `git show <rev>:.github/firstrun.yml`, then `.firstrun.yml`, with a 30 s timeout. A missing file is fine.

## F. Privacy and ethics

**What is shown:**
- The git author name, already public in commits and already on boards via `features[].author`.
- The GitHub login and the avatar from GitHub.
- Commit counts and dates.

**What is never shown:**
- Emails, whether raw or hashed: hashes of emails can be reversed against Gravatar-style lookups.
- Person ids are `p1` to `pN`.

`team.sanitize(doc)` runs in `publish()` and `intake.validate()`:
- Drop any string field matching `[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.-]+`.
- Enforce the login regex and an integer `gh`.
- Cap list sizes: people 16, areas 12, items 30.
- Drop unknown keys in `team`.

**Opt-outs:**
- Run level: `--no-team` or `FIRSTRUN_TEAM=0`.
- Repo owner: put `team: false` in `.github/firstrun.yml` or `.firstrun.yml` (regex parse, no YAML dependency).
- Requester: the issue template gets a checkbox, "Leave out the team map (contributor names and avatars)". `intake.parse_issue` returns `team: False` when it is ticked.
- Person: add `"sha256:<hex of lowercase login, or normalized name>"` to `hidden` in `docs/audits/team-optout.json` (`{"v":1,"hidden":[],"bots":["fa-assistant"]}`), then run the backfill with `--force --only`. A hidden person's weight moves into `others`, and they are never suggested. The file stores hashes so it does not publish a list of who opted out.

**Wording:**
- The team note: "Built from public commits in the last 12 months. Suggestions, not assignments: anyone can pick up any task."
- Labels say "Suggested", never "Assigned".

**Private repos:**
- They stay local as today, and `team` is computed for the owner's `runs/` report.
- `audit-submit` strips `team` and the owner, runner-up and fallback fields from `next` unless `--with-team` is passed, and it says so in its prompt.

**README:** add a "Team map and privacy" subsection under section 7.

**`docs/known-limits.md`:**
- Identities merge by login only when a token is available.
- Co-author trailers are ignored. AI co-author trailers are common, and human pairing trailers are rare.
- Weights use files, not lines.

## B. Team: identity, expertise, areas

**New module: `src/firstrun/team.py`**

### B1. History fields (additive, in `audit.py`)

- `read_history(repo, rev="HEAD")` uses the format `%x01%H%x09%cI%x09%aI%x09%P%x09%an%x09%ae%x09%s` and `split("\t", 6)`.
- It adds the keys `email`, `adate` (author date) and `parents` (count). `date`, `author`, `subject`, `files` and `scope` stay unchanged.
- `read_tags` adds `tagger` (`%(taggername)`). It stays empty for lightweight tags.
- Emails are used only inside `team.py` and are never written anywhere.

### B2. Which commits count

A commit counts only if all of these hold:
- `parents <= 1` (merges are skipped).
- `adate` is within 365 days of `as_of`.
- The author is not a bot.
- It touches 300 files or fewer. Bigger commits are mass imports, formatting runs or Copybara drops ("Project import generated by Copybara." is in dbt).

Files are dropped by `TEAM_SKIP`:
- Hidden dirs: `(^|/)\.[^/]+/`. This covers `.github`, `.changes`, `.claude`, `.changeset`.
- `(^|/)(node_modules|vendor|third_party|dist|build|out|target)/`
- Lockfiles and snapshots: `\.lock$`, `-lock\.json$`, `lock\.ya?ml$`, `go\.sum$`, `\.snap$`
- Generated files: `\.min\.(js|css)$`, `\.pb\.go$`, `_pb2\.py$`
- `(^|/)(changelog|changes|history)(\.[a-z]+)?$` (case-insensitive)

### B3. Bots

`is_bot(name, email, login)` is true if any of these match:
- Login, email local part, or name ends with `[bot]`.
- Login or email local part ends with `bot`. So does a name with no spaces (this catches `dependabot`, `FishtownBuildBot`, `snyk-bot`). A spaced name like "Sam Talbot" is safe.
- Lowercased name or login is in a known list: `github-actions, dependabot, renovate, copilot, copilot-swe-agent, pre-commit-ci, greenkeeper, codecov, mergify, semantic-release-bot, allcontributors, claude, devin-ai-integration, cursoragent, codex, web-flow`.
- Email is `noreply@github.com`, `actions@github.com`, or `*@anthropic.com` when the name is Claude.
- Login, or a name with no spaces, matches `(^|[-_])(assistant|automation)$`. This catches `fa-assistant`.
- Login or name is in `bots` of `docs/audits/team-optout.json` (see F).

### B4. Identity and merging

Parse emails:
- `^(\d+)\+([^@]+)@users\.noreply\.github\.com$` → gh id and login.
- `^([^@+]+)@users\.noreply\.github\.com$` → login.

When a token exists, run the GitHub lookup:
- Take the newest commit sha of each identity (distinct lowercased email). Limit this to the top 100 identities by weight.
- Query `https://api.github.com/graphql` in batches of 50: `c{i}: object(oid:"<hex>"){... on Commit{author{user{login databaseId}}}}`, with `repository(owner,name)` taken from the clone URL. Validate that each oid is hex.
- Token: `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GH_TOKEN`, else `gh auth token` (subprocess, 5 s timeout, never logged).
- Each call uses `httpx` with a 15 s timeout. Stop after 4 calls. Skip the lookup if the `X-RateLimit-Remaining` header is under 50.
- Any exception returns `{}` and sets `source = "git"`. Keep an in-process memo only and no disk cache: at most 4 calls per audit, so a cache adds risk and saves nothing.

Merge identities with union-find:
- Same login, or same lowercased email.
- Same normalized name: NFKD, accents stripped, casefold, punctuation removed, whitespace collapsed. Skip the name merge when the two identities have different known logins, or the name is generic (`root, admin, ubuntu, user, unknown, github, dev`).

Display values:
- Name: the most-used git name. If it contains `@`, use the login. If there is no login, use `Contributor N`.
- `ini`: first letters of the first two name tokens, else the first two characters of the login.

Without a token, "Victor Gutierrez" and "Victor Gutierrez Calderon" (entireio) stay separate. With a token they merge through the login `gtrrz-victor`. That is acceptable.

### B5. Recency-weighted file weight

```
decay(c)  = 2 ** (-(as_of - c.adate).days / 90)
n         = len(kept_files(c))
mass(c)   = decay(c) * min(1 + log2(n), 4)       # 1 file = 1, 2 = 2, 4 = 3, 8 or more = 4
share(c,f)= mass(c) / n                          # spread evenly over the commit's files
```

Why these numbers:
- **Half-life 90 days.** A quarter is the usual planning cycle. A one-year-old commit counts 6%, so people who left fade out and steady contributors stay.
- **Window 365 days.** Older commits weigh under 6%. Cutting them keeps the run fast.
- **Log cap.** A 250-file refactor counts at most 4 one-file fixes, spread thinly. No single commit can dominate.
- **Files, not lines.** Line counts need blobs, which the clone does not have.

Accumulate:
- `w[p][f]` per file.
- `dw[p][(repo, dir)]` for every ancestor dir, up to depth 6.

### B6. Areas: the "frontier" split (decided, replaces `features[].area` for the team)

Inputs:
- `file_w[(repo, path)]`, summed over all humans.
- The set of dirs present at `as_of` (`git ls-tree -r --name-only <rev>`).

A path whose dir no longer exists maps to its longest existing ancestor. If it has none, it goes to `rest`. That also handles renames.

```
DESCEND = 0.85; SPLIT = 0.22; MIN = 0.03; AREAS_MAX = 10 (single repo) | code 7 + docs 3 (docs repo)
descend(n): while n has a child c with W(c) >= DESCEND*W(n): n = c       # skips src/, packages/x/src/, crates/
nodes = [descend(c) for c in children(root) if W(c) >= MIN*T]; root-level files and small children go to rest
loop:
  n = heaviest node with W(n) >= SPLIT*T and at least 2 child dirs with W >= MIN*T
  if none or len(nodes) >= AREAS_MAX: break
  replace n with [descend(c) for those children] + "n (other)" bucket if the remainder is >= MIN*T, else the remainder goes to rest
keep the heaviest AREAS_MAX nodes; the rest go to rest
label = basename(n); if basename is in {src, lib, app, core, internal, pkg, main, source, packages, crates, docs, content}: use "parent/basename"
```

When `docs_repo` is set, run the frontier separately per repo: `repo:"code"` with up to 7 areas and `repo:"docs"` with up to 3. Shares are within each repo. People merge across both repos by login or normalized name. In a single repo, docs dirs compete as normal areas (for accuknox: `docs/use-cases`, `docs/getting-started`, and so on).

### B7. Per-area and per-person metrics

| Field | Formula |
|---|---|
| `area.share` | `W(area) / T(repo)` |
| `owners[].s` | person's weight in the area / `W(area)`, over all humans, with `others` aggregated |
| `bus` | smallest k such that the top-k owner shares sum to at least 0.5 (classic truck factor) |
| `single` | top share >= 0.75, or only one person with share >= 0.05 |
| `quiet` | `as_of - area.last` > 180 days |
| `person.share` | person's weight / total human weight |
| `top` | the person's heaviest area |
| `top_share` | that area's weight / the person's total weight (including `rest`) |
| `commits`, `last` | raw counts and dates, shown to humans; ranking uses weights |

Why a truck factor and not the suggested ">20% holders" count: with ten people at 10% each, the >20% rule gives a bus factor of 0, which is wrong. Taking the fewest people who hold half the work stays meaningful at any team size.

Which people are listed:
- The top 12 by weight, and only those with share >= 1.5% or at least 3 commits.
- Everyone else goes into `others`.
- Owners and runners-up from `next` are appended, up to 16 in total.

Edge cases:
- **One person:** 1 person, every area `single`. The UI says so plainly (D).
- **1 to 3 people:** normal map.
- **Hundreds of people:** top 12 plus `others`. Test this at 300.
- **History capped at 20,000:** if the oldest commit is newer than the window start, set `team.capped = true`.

`build_team(sources, as_of, hidden=set(), extra_bots=set(), token=None) -> (team_json, ctx)`. The `ctx`, which is internal and never serialized, holds:
- `pid_of_sha[sha9]`
- `files_of_sha[sha9]`
- `dw`
- `recent_by_dir[(repo, dir)]`: the newest 20 human commits, as `(pid, date)`
- `last_toucher(repo, path) -> (name, date)`
- `active(pid)`: true if the last commit is within 180 days
- `momentum`

## C. Top 10 prioritized items with rationale

**New module: `src/firstrun/nextup.py`**

`build_next(board, ctx | None, as_of, mom, changelog_recent) -> dict`. Inputs are only what a board already holds (`cards`, `pages`, `features`, `release`) plus history. That makes new audits and the backfill share the same code.

### C1. Candidates

- Every non-`content` card, mapped by kind.
- Up to 10 extra `refresh` candidates: stale or unchecked pages not already in a refresh card, top by `relevant_since`. Their evidence is `page.evidence`.
- Join a refresh card to its page by path (the `Refresh <path>` title, or `cardPath` logic). Join features by `sha`.
- Join document clusters to all `features` with the same `area` and `covered == false`.
- Dedupe announces by cleaned subject; accuknox has "Add GCP organization onboarding guide" twice. Drop an announce whose sha already appears in a document item.

### C2. Score

All parts are in [0, 1]. `d(x)` means days between `as_of` and date `x`.

```
score = round(100 * (0.30*I + 0.25*U + 0.20*E + 0.15*J + 0.10*ease)),  ease: S=1, M=0.6, L=0.3

document cluster: I = 0.55 + 0.25*min(1, n/10) + 0.20*min(1, mom[area].commits/30)
                  U = 2**(-d(newest)/45)
                  E = min(1, n/5) * (1 if area_src == "scope" or any strong term else 0.85)
                  J = 1 if any feature.judge == "jev" else 0.6
document single:  I = 0.55 + 0.10*(has strong term)
                  U = 2**(-d/45)
                  E = 0.6 + 0.2*(strong term) + 0.2*(PR number)
                  J as above
refresh:          I = 0.45 + 0.25*entry(path) + 0.30*min(1, relevant_since/20)
                  U = 0.5*min(1, age_days/730) + 0.5*2**(-d(newest evidence)/90)
                  E = min(1, relevant_since/5)
                  J = 1 if judge == "jev" and status == "stale"; 0.6 if text only; 0.35 if unchecked
                  entry = 1 if the name matches readme|index|quickstart|getting[-_]started|install|introduction|overview, or path depth <= 2
release:          I = 0.5 + 0.15*(not changelog_recent); U = 2**(-d(release.date)/30)
                  E = min(1, commits/10); J = 0.6
                  skip when commits == 0
announce:         I = 0.25; U = 2**(-d/21); E = 0.5 + 0.2*(PR); J = 0.4
quickstart:       I = 0.4 + 0.3*(README or quickstart-like page is stale/unchecked/aging)
                  U = 0.3; E = 0.3; J = 0.5
```

Why the weights are ordered this way:
1. **Impact first:** docs exist for readers.
2. **Urgency second:** users are trying new features now, and a stale page misleads every visitor today.
3. **Evidence third:** prefer what can be proven.
4. **Judged fourth:** a model read the page, versus a text match.
5. **Ease last:** a tie-breaker that favors quick wins without letting trivia outrank real gaps.

Hand-checked against real boards:

| Board | Item | Score |
|---|---|---|
| altimate-code | `workspace` cluster | 92 |
| dbt-core | `databricks` cluster | 85 |
| dbt-core | `_versions-contracts.md` refresh | 82 |
| accuknox | `Process-based-asset-access` refresh | 72 |
| altimate-code | YOLO single | 67 |
| (any) | announce | about 55 |
| accuknox | `net-seg` refresh | 50 |

**Effort rules** (`effort_why` gives the rule in words):

| Kind | S | M | L |
|---|---|---|---|
| refresh | `relevant_since` <= 3 | <= 10 | more than 10 |
| document cluster, own page exists | | n <= 6 | otherwise |
| document cluster, new page | | otherwise | n >= 8 |
| document single | has `closest_page` | otherwise | |
| release, announce, quickstart | always | | |

For refresh, an `ancient` page moves up one level, capped at L.

**Order and caps:**
- Sort by score descending, then newest evidence, then title.
- Caps inside the top 10: refresh 5, document 5, announce 2, release 1, quickstart 1.
- Overflow continues at rank 11 and later. Keep at most 30 items.

### C3. Text, from real fields only

**Titles:**
- Cluster with its own page: "Add the new {area} changes to {basename}".
- Cluster with no page: "Write a page for {area}".
- Single: "Document: {Clean subject}".
- Refresh: "Update {page title}", with `path` set.
- Release: "Publish the {name} release notes".
- Announce: "Announce: {Clean subject}".
- Quickstart: "Prove the quickstart still runs".

**Rationale** (one sentence, always citing a SHA, a date or a count):
- Refresh: "Last edited {date}. Since then {k} commits changed code on its topic, newest {sha} on {date}, and Jev expects the page is now wrong." The last clause is "Jev did not read it" when Jev did not run.
- Single: "{sha} shipped "{subject}" on {date} in #{pr}, and Jev read {closest_page} and found it does not explain it."
- Release: "{n} commits landed between {prev} and {name} ({date}), and no changelog file changed in the last 60 days."
- Cluster: as in the schema example.

**why_now:**
- Document and announce: "Shipped 4 days ago", "Shipped 3 weeks ago", "Shipped 2 months ago".
- Refresh: "Code moved 32 days ago under a page last edited 680 days ago".
- Release: "v2.0.5 shipped 3 days ago".
- Quickstart: "A text audit cannot prove a run".

### C4. Owner suggestion

```
For each item, collect:
  code_dirs: parent dirs of the product files in its evidence commits (found by sha in history), plus feature.files
  docs_dir:  parent dir of path (refresh), closest_page (document), README (quickstart)
A(p) = share of the item's evidence commits authored by p
C(p) = sum over d in code_dirs of dw[p][d] / max over q of the same     (0 for everyone if that max < 1.0)
D(p) = dw[p][docs_dir], plus the file itself, / max over q              (same floor)
aff  = a*A + b*C + g*D, with (a, b, g):
       document (.50, .35, .15)   refresh (.25, .30, .45)   announce (.80, .20, 0)
       quickstart (0, 0, 1)
       release: if the newest tag's tagger is human, that person gets aff 1; otherwise A over the release range
eligible = active in the last 180 days
owner only if top aff >= 0.25
otherwise owner = null and fallback = last human toucher of path or evidence files:
       "Last touched by {name} on {date}", else "No one touched these files in the last year"
```

**Load balancing** applies to the top 10 only, in rank order:
- `cap = max(2, ceil(10 / n_eligible) + 1)`, where `n_eligible` counts people with aff >= 0.25 on any top item. There is no cap when `n_eligible <= 1`.
- The pool is the eligible people with `aff >= 0.6 * top_aff`. Pick the first one in the pool whose load is under the cap. If none, pick the top expert anyway: the cap is soft.
- Set `balanced = true` when the pick is not the top expert.
- `runner_up` is the best other eligible person with aff >= 0.15.

**Reason** (the strongest term wins):
- A: "{name} shipped it in #{pr}" or "{name} wrote {k} of the {n} changes behind it".
- C or D: "{name} made {k} of the last {m} commits to {dir}/". `dir` is the deepest ancestor with at least 5 window commits. `m = min(20, commits to dir)`.
- Release: "{name} tagged {tag}".

Each item's `area` is the area whose path is the longest prefix of the item's primary file.

## D. UI spec (`docs/doc-audit/index.html`)

### D1. Choice of visualization

I rejected these options:
- **Chord diagram:** unreadable to a stranger and bad at 375 px.
- **Classic Sankey:** small nodes make labels collide.
- **Avatar bubbles:** imprecise.
- **Swimlane:** reads like a log.
- **Heatmap:** precise but needs a color legend.

**Primary view (760 px and wider): tapered ribbon map.** It is three aligned columns: a people list in HTML, an SVG ribbon band, and an areas list in HTML.
- Every row has a fixed 52 px pitch, and every node bar is 36 px tall, so labels never collide.
- A ribbon's **left end** thickness is the share of that person's work ("X works most on Y").
- Its **right end** thickness is that person's share of the area ("who holds Y").

One shape answers both questions. The only key is two column headers: "People · share of their work" and "Parts of the code · share of the area".

**Secondary view (default and only view under 760 px): "By area" list.**
- One row per area: label, the path in faint mono, and a 12 px stacked ownership bar in person colors, with others in gray.
- Under the bar: owner avatars with percentages.
- A badge: "1 owner" (warn style) when `single`, otherwise "{bus} hold half".
- It is semantic HTML, so it also serves as a text equivalent.

Order: header, `.health` bar, then a new `<section id="r-team" class="tband">`, then "What to Ship Next".

### E1. Backfill script: `scripts/audit_team_backfill.py` (same style as `audit_cost_estimates.py`)

Options:

2. `rev = history.head`, or `git rev-list -1 --before=<generated_at> HEAD`.
3. `commits = read_history(repo, rev)` and `tags = read_tags`. Get the paths at `rev` with `ls-tree`. Do the same for `docs_repo`.

5. `mom = audit.momentum(commits, as_of, board["features"])`. Compute `changelog_recent` the way `_audit` does.
6. Build `team` and `next`.
7. Set `b2 = {**b, "team": ..., "next": ...}`. Assert that `set(b2) - set(b) <= {"team", "next"}` and that every other value is equal.

## F. Privacy and ethics

**What is shown:**
- The git author name, already public in commits and already on boards via `features[].author`.
- The GitHub login and the avatar from GitHub.
- Commit counts and dates.

**What is never shown:**
- Emails, whether raw or hashed: hashes of emails can be reversed against Gravatar-style lookups.
- Person ids are `p1` to `pN`.

`team.sanitize(doc)` runs in `publish()` and `intake.validate()`:
- Drop any string field matching `[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.-]+`.
- Enforce the login regex and an integer `gh`.
- Cap list sizes: people 16, areas 12, items 30.
- Drop unknown keys in `team`.

**Opt-outs:**
- Run level: `--no-team` or `FIRSTRUN_TEAM=0`.
- Repo owner: put `team: false` in `.github/firstrun.yml` or `.firstrun.yml` (regex parse, no YAML dependency).
- Requester: the issue template gets a checkbox, "Leave out the team map (contributor names and avatars)". `intake.parse_issue` returns `team: False` when it is ticked.
- Person: add `"sha256:<hex of lowercase login, or normalized name>"` to `hidden` in `docs/audits/team-optout.json` (`{"v":1,"hidden":[],"bots":["fa-assistant"]}`), then run the backfill with `--force --only`. A hidden person's weight moves into `others`, and they are never suggested. The file stores hashes so it does not publish a list of who opted out.

**Wording:**
- The team note: "Built from public commits in the last 12 months. Suggestions, not assignments: anyone can pick up any task."
- Labels say "Suggested", never "Assigned".

**Private repos:**
- They stay local as today, and `team` is computed for the owner's `runs/` report.
- `audit-submit` strips `team` and the owner, runner-up and fallback fields from `next` unless `--with-team` is passed, and it says so in its prompt.

**README:** add a "Team map and privacy" subsection under section 7.

**`docs/known-limits.md`:**
- Identities merge by login only when a token is available.
- Co-author trailers are ignored. AI co-author trailers are common, and human pairing trailers are rare.
- Weights use files, not lines.

content.text:
The planning session is done, and I saved the plan. The two builder agents are now running in parallel. Nothing has come back from either yet.

**What the plan decided**
- **Top 10 list.** It replaces the weak "Create Content" column with one ranked list. Each item has a score from five weighted signals: reader impact, urgency, evidence strength, whether Jev checked it, and effort. Each item also gets a one-sentence rationale that cites commits and dates, an effort size, and a suggested owner.
- **Team map.** It builds a tapered ribbon visual. People are on the left and parts of the code on the right. A ribbon's thickness shows how much of that person's work is there, and how much of that area they hold. Hover a person to light up their areas and their suggested tasks. Click to filter the list to their picks.
- **Safety.**
  - Bots are excluded.
  - Emails are never shown.
  - A failed GitHub lookup never fails an audit.
  - Suggestions are labeled "Suggested", never "Assigned".
  - There are three opt-outs: a CLI flag, a repo file, and an issue checkbox.

**One call for you, because it publishes named people.** The 7 published boards include third-party repos (dbt-labs, fastapi/typer, entireio, OrchestratorInc). The map would show real contributor names and GitHub avatars from their public commits. The default in the plan is to publish them, framed as suggestions with an opt-out. Say "no third-party maps" before I merge and I limit the maps to your own repos.

**Running now (7 jobs)**
1. The prism hero and navbar.
2. The tool evidence section.
3. The audit cost re-runs.
4. The team map data and algorithm.
5. The team map visuals.
6. The Top 10 list, which is part of 4 and 5.

I merge everything together when all of it is done.

Next: tell me about the third-party maps, or leave it and I use the default.
