## Where I departed from the plan
**The frontend agent must know these two before it renders:**
- `cells` weights are a percent of all work in the window, to 2 decimals. The plan did not set a unit.
- `area.share` is relative to that area's own repo. `rest.share` is relative to all repos combined.

**Changes to the algorithm, each made because real output looked wrong:**
- **Area split:** a folder also splits when it has one big subfolder plus a remainder of at least 3%. On orchestrator, a deleted `landing/` folder left a single 44% "frontend/src" area. It now splits into components, renderer and i18n.
- **Code-folder affinity:** each folder counts only the files directly in it, is scored on its own (best person = 1), and is weighted by how many of the item's files sit there. Summing subtree weights gave entireio's "agent" item to Stefan Haubold because one file sat in the flat `cli/` package. Hidde Beydals, who wrote 2 of the 3 changes, now gets it.
- **Docs floor:** lowered from 1.0 to 0.5. Under 1.0, no README ever had an owner.
- **Release ownership:** counted over commits made by people only, because ranges are mostly bot commits (typer: 1 human commit in 19). Ties go to the person with more overall weight. The reason reads "wrote k of the n commits people made in TAG".
- **Commits that carry no weight** (over 300 files, or only skipped files) still record who wrote them. Without this, accuknox said "No one touched these files in the last year" for a recent commit. When nobody in the window touched the files, the fallback names the author of the newest evidence commit.
- **Reasons:** when the board lists fewer changes than the real count, they say "of the N changes the board lists for it". The folder reason picks the folder where the person has the largest share of the last 20 commits. A new reason, "made k of the m edits to README.md", covers single files.
- `item.area` is the area that holds most of the item's code files. The first file alone can sit in a side folder.
- If the per-kind caps leave fewer than 10 items in the top 10, the gap is filled from overflow and the 10 are re-sorted by score.

**Smaller changes:**
- **Bots:** a "bot" suffix needs a separator or a capital B, so "Talbot" and "Abbot" stay people.
- **Lock files:** the pattern is `(^|[/-])lock\.ya?ml$`, so `block.yaml` is not skipped.
- **Scores:** parts are rounded to 2 decimals before scoring, so anyone can recompute a score from the published parts.
- **Size guards:** `next` drops its lowest ranks past 10 until it is under 24.5 KB, and items past rank 10 keep 3 evidence rows. dbt went from 34.7 KB with 30 items to 23.5 KB with 19. `team` drops its thinnest cells above 9.8 KB.
- **Signatures:** `build_team` gained `github=` and `release=` arguments.
- **Fallback:** `fallback` is null when there is an owner, and null for a release with no owner.
- **Release title:** "Unreleased" gets "Publish release notes for the last 30 days".
- **Not done:** `ctx.momentum` is not implemented, because nothing reads it.

## Known weaknesses
- **dbt docs areas are coarse.** website/docs holds 76% of docs work, because the plan caps docs at 3 areas.
- **Some owner reasons are weak, though true.** Examples: "3 of the last 20 commits to cmd/entire/cli/" and "luna-bianca made 1 of the last 20 commits".
- **Some items have no owner:**
  - dbt "Debug Snapshot" refresh: the docs folder weight is under the floor, although James Waller touched the page on Sep 26.
  - neatlogs and accuknox release items: no person made a weighted commit in those ranges. The accuknox tag is named "cdr-test".
  - accuknox quickstart: the README weight is under the floor.
- **Lightweight tags have no tagger,** so typer's release owner comes from commit authorship instead.
- **Opt-out file reach:** `team-optout.json` is found only inside this checkout. A pip-installed CI run in another repo has no per-person opt-outs.
- **Trimmed items can leave extra people:** if items past rank 10 are dropped for size, their owners may stay on the map with no pick.
- **Without a token,** identities merge only by noreply login, email or name.

## Where I departed from the plan
**The frontend agent must know these two before it renders:**
- `cells` weights are a percent of all work in the window, to 2 decimals. The plan did not set a unit.
- `area.share` is relative to that area's own repo. `rest.share` is relative to all repos combined.

**Changes to the algorithm, each made because real output looked wrong:**
- **Area split:** a folder also splits when it has one big subfolder plus a remainder of at least 3%. On orchestrator, a deleted `landing/` folder left a single 44% "frontend/src" area. It now splits into components, renderer and i18n.
- **Code-folder affinity:** each folder counts only the files directly in it, is scored on its own (best person = 1), and is weighted by how many of the item's files sit there. Summing subtree weights gave entireio's "agent" item to Stefan Haubold because one file sat in the flat `cli/` package. Hidde Beydals, who wrote 2 of the 3 changes, now gets it.
- **Docs floor:** lowered from 1.0 to 0.5. Under 1.0, no README ever had an owner.
- **Release ownership:** counted over commits made by people only, because ranges are mostly bot commits (typer: 1 human commit in 19). Ties go to the person with more overall weight. The reason reads "wrote k of the n commits people made in TAG".
- **Commits that carry no weight** (over 300 files, or only skipped files) still record who wrote them. Without this, accuknox said "No one touched these files in the last year" for a recent commit. When nobody in the window touched the files, the fallback names the author of the newest evidence commit.
- **Reasons:** when the board lists fewer changes than the real count, they say "of the N changes the board lists for it". The folder reason picks the folder where the person has the largest share of the last 20 commits. A new reason, "made k of the m edits to README.md", covers single files.
- `item.area` is the area that holds most of the item's code files. The first file alone can sit in a side folder.
- If the per-kind caps leave fewer than 10 items in the top 10, the gap is filled from overflow and the 10 are re-sorted by score.

**Smaller changes:**
- **Bots:** a "bot" suffix needs a separator or a capital B, so "Talbot" and "Abbot" stay people.
- **Lock files:** the pattern is `(^|[/-])lock\.ya?ml$`, so `block.yaml` is not skipped.
- **Scores:** parts are rounded to 2 decimals before scoring, so anyone can recompute a score from the published parts.
- **Size guards:** `next` drops its lowest ranks past 10 until it is under 24.5 KB, and items past rank 10 keep 3 evidence rows. dbt went from 34.7 KB with 30 items to 23.5 KB with 19. `team` drops its thinnest cells above 9.8 KB.
- **Signatures:** `build_team` gained `github=` and `release=` arguments.
- **Fallback:** `fallback` is null when there is an owner, and null for a release with no owner.
- **Release title:** "Unreleased" gets "Publish release notes for the last 30 days".

content.content:
```bash firstrun audit dbt-labs/dbt-core --docs-repo dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com ``` One blobless clone gives the whole history. The audit then works offline and costs $0 in model calls. Jev sorts commits with no conventional prefix when `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is set, and every audit is one neatlogs trace. - **Oldest first.** Every page, ranked by the date of its last edit. - **Stale or quiet.** A page is stale when product commits on its topic landed after its last edit, and the report names those commits. An old page that nothing changed under is quiet, so the team can leave it alone. - **Features with no docs.** Each user-facing commit in 120 days is checked against the docs text. A flag or name that no page mentions becomes a "Document this" card. - **Proposal cards.** Document this, refresh this page, feature this, and automate the release notes. - **What to ship next.** One ranked list of up to 30 tasks. Each task has a score from 0 to 100, an effort of S, M or L, and one sentence that cites the commits and dates behind it. The score adds reader impact, urgency, evidence, whether Jev checked it, and e - **Who works on what.** A map of the people who made the last 12 months of commits and the parts of the code they work on. Each task suggests an owner and gives the reason, such as "Maya made 14 of the last 20 commits to docs/use-cases/". - **Drafts.** Release notes for the newest stable tag and up to 3 product highlights, written from commit subjects and pull request numbers. `firstrun audit-issue` turns the newest audit into `issue.md`, one checkbox for each of the top 10 tasks, and prints the `gh issue create` command. It opens nothing on its own. A suggested owner appears as a name and a login without the @, so nobody gets a Git **Team map and privacy.** The map reads public commits: author names, GitHub logins and avatars, commit counts and dates. It never shows an email, raw or hashed. Emails stay in memory to join one person's commits, and a sanitizer drops any email before a board Bots are left out. A commit counts by the files it changed, never by lines, and a commit 90 days old counts half. Every owner is a suggestion, not an assignment. Four opt-outs turn the map off or hide one person: - Run `firstrun audit --no-team`, or set `FIRSTRUN_TEAM=0`. - A repo owner adds `team: false` to `.github/firstrun.yml` or `.firstrun.yml`. - An audit request ticks "Leave out the team map" on the issue form. `firstrun audit-submit` leaves the map out unless you add `--with-team`. - A person adds `sha256:` of their lowercase login or name to `hidden` in [`docs/audits/team-optout.json`](docs/audits/team-optout.json). Their work moves into "Everyone else" and no task suggests them. To audit every week, copy [`examples/github-action/firstrun-audit.yml`](examples/github-action/firstrun-audit.yml) into `.github/workflows/`. Each Monday it audits the repo and updates one issue labeled `firstrun-audit`, so the docs team gets a fresh work list ...... ### cfo.ai Prices the Nightly Check

Ari, the cfo.ai agent, on day one.		 The business plan sets the agent's spending limit. `firstrun econ` reads 88 neatlogs traces and writes [business/drivers.csv](business/drivers.csv) for cfo.ai. The mean run costs $0.0178, and the p95 | Tier | Price | Quickstarts | Cap per run | Runs over the cap | |---|---|---|---|---| | Free | $0 | 1, weekly | $0.0135 | 50.0% | | Team | $49 a month | 10, nightly | $0.0470 | 9.1% | | Scale | $299 a month | 100, nightly, with PRs, Bisect and Prerequisite Proof | $0.0279 | 26.1% | The old fixed cap of $0.50 let one bad month cost a Scale customer's fee five times over. The plan, the Scale fix and every assumption are in [business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md](business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md). Th The [plan page](https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/plan/) shows the caps, the measured cost spread and the cash per Scenario. Every doc-test run is tagged against the caps. Set-Location D:\Atharva\firstrun
git add README.md business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md docs/judges/index.html evidence/README.md evidence/entire.md hackathon.md docs/audits/audit-*.json
git status --short | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch '^\?\?' } | ForEach-Object { $_ } | Select-Object -First 20
$msg = Join-Path $env:TEMP "launch_msg.txt"
@"
Launch batch: team map and top 10 data for the 7 audits, receipts docs, corrected counts

Adds the team and next blocks to the 7 published audit boards with
scripts/audit_team_backfill.py (only those two keys changed, no emails).
Documents receipts and the judges page in the README and the evidence index.
Corrects stale figures: 75 of 113 non-merge commits carry an Entire
checkpoint trailer, 88 traces back the cost drivers, the cfo.ai scenario
table matches the export, and the offline suite is 360 tests.
"@ | Set-Content $msg -Encoding utf8
& "C:\Users\AtharvaShah\.local\bin\entire.exe" hooks git prepare-commit-msg $msg message
Get-Content $msg | Select-Object -Last 3
$p = Start-Process git -ArgumentList @('commit','-F',$msg) -PassThru -NoNewWindow -RedirectStandardOutput "$env:TEMP\c_out.txt" -RedirectStandardError "$env:TEMP\c_err.txt"
$t0 = Get-Date
while (-not $p.HasExited -and ((Get-Date) - $t0).TotalSeconds -lt 120) {
  Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 1500
  Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='entire.exe'" | ForEach-Object { if ($_.CommandLine -match 'prepare-commit-msg') { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force } }
}
"commit exit=$($p.ExitCode)"
git log --oneline -1
git log -1 --format=%B | Select-String "Entire-Checkpoint"
